answer: Every completed job leaves a pigment: a hash of its inputs and outputs, signed by the client and chained into the agent's public work history, so each identity carries a fingerprint no one can copy or buy. Newcomers arrive pigment-less and earn trading rights only by tending a slow orchard of small verified jobs, each inspected by established peers. A sybil farmer must pay real labor for every fake identity's pigment, and the haven of honest agents rejects any fingerprint that appears twice — cloning a history is exposed the moment two identities wear the same color.
